Summary: Single OpenAI-compatible endpoint for all model calls
Description: Provider abstraction, per-key scoping, budgets and rate limits so apps point at one governed URL instead of providers directly.
Add/list/delete provider keys (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Mistral, xAI, OpenRouter); AES-256 encrypted at rest; plaintext never returned after creation.
Bind provider+model+API key under a slug; slug is the client-facing model. Model in LiteLLM format.
Issue sk-vw- keys decoupled from provider keys; per-key allowed endpoints, model/provider ACLs, budget, rate limit; shown once, SHA-256 stored.
Proxy /v1/chat/completions and /v1/embeddings via LiteLLM; streaming and non-streaming.
Forward tool definitions so agents can do tool-calling through the gateway.
Fail over to a fallback endpoint on provider error.
Per-org/per-key spend caps (402) and request limits (429); monthly budget reset; rejections logged.
Support multi-field provider credentials (Azure endpoint+version+deployment, Vertex project+location+SA JSON, Bedrock keys+region).

Summary: Proxy & audit every agent tool call
Description: Govern what agents do (tools), not just what they say (LLM), through registered MCP servers with agent-key auth and a full audit trail.
Admin registers Streamable-HTTP MCP servers (name, slug, url, auth_type); per-server health status.
Discover calls tools/list and upserts tools into the registry; deactivates removed tools.
sk-mcp- keys with allowed/blocked tools, allowed servers, rate limit; shown once, SHA-256 stored.
Streamable-HTTP JSON-RPC (initialize, tools/list, tools/call) proxied to the correct backend with session management.
Set REDIS_URL so MCP sessions work in Docker (was defaulting to localhost).
Log every tool call (tool, agent key, args, result status, latency); stats by-tool and by-agent.
requires_approval tools return an approval request; admin approves/denies; per-tool input guardrails.
Request inspection that blocks or masks before the model is reached; enforced at the gateway so every agent inherits it.
Rules with keyword/regex patterns; block or mask. Verified self-harm regex blocks (400), clean prompt passes.
Entity detection (CREDIT_CARD, EMAIL_ADDRESS, ...) with per-entity block/mask. Verified card blocked, email masked.
Regex rule blocks ignore-previous-instructions / reveal-system-prompt / developer-mode attempts.
Log every detection (type, action, entity, matched text); aggregate stats by type/day.
Scan and block/mask the model response, not just the request.
Org setting to enable/disable request/response body capture for privacy-sensitive clients.
Per-request logging plus dashboards turning runtime telemetry into operational and audit insight (cost, usage, safety, per-user).
Each call logs provider, model, tokens, cost, latency, status, metadata.
Fix jsonb/array casts that broke spend logging and virtual-key creation under asyncpg.
Store guardrail-scanned request messages + response text (bounded); expandable in UI; requester via x-vw-metadata; system prompts hidden.
Totals (cost/requests/tokens), avg & P95 latency, error rate, cache hit rate; by endpoint/user/tag; period filters.
Cost per client/agent, budget utilization + alerts, 429/402 counts, PII-by-type, per-agent tool latency & blocks, spend anomaly flag.
Persist rate-limit/budget rejections so they are countable in insights.
Read-only service API key + stable /metrics and logs endpoints for Vector AI / SIEM ingestion; webhooks on block/budget events.
Configurable retention (days) and purge for spend/guardrail/audit logs.
Make onboarding a config step; any agent (basic script or multi-agent system) is governed the moment it routes through the gateway.
Documented flow: provider key -> endpoint -> virtual key -> set base_url+key+slug. Validated with OpenAI SDK, LangChain, Google ADK.
x-vw-metadata header carries app/agent/user; surfaces in logs and spend/by-tag.

Summary: AIONIQ chat UI with Google Sign-In
Description: FastAPI wrapper verifies Google ID token server-side; per-user agent attaches verified email to gateway calls; chat UI with streaming + guardrail-block messaging.
ADK/LangGraph agents connect tools via /v1/mcp with an agent key; calls appear in MCP audit.
End-to-end HTML guide: keys -> endpoints -> virtual keys -> connect -> guardrails -> MCP -> logs, with gotchas reference.
Entra ID sign-in option on the agent chat (platform Entra SSO already enabled; extend to the agent wrapper).
